reason: The local gate is the per-change proof for built executables.
The companion test module is compile-checked on every build gate.
Container tests run in the local build gate; release adds the full round trip.
Existing vet debt is a shrink-only set baseline in the local gate.
The GUI's separate self-test is part of the local build gate when GUI is built.
Preflight verifies tools, anchors, the stamped build and the full fdsec round trip before tagging.
The registry is checked on every local build gate.
Frozen winget anchors are checked before a tag and synced manifests before submit.
CI re-hashes all release assets before publishing them.
The tag workflow builds and smoke-checks the staged release artifacts.
WACK and the published privacy URL are pre-submission checks requiring an elevated operator session.
Listing and manifest tooling are run by the Store operator when Store copy or tooling changes.
Packed-manifest and stamp assertions run while building the Store submission package.
Scenario lists are operator-driven checks; their paths are placeholders the runner fills from FILEDO_TEST_TARGET, which must name a mounted VHD or a folder under %TEMP%.
The vendored glyphs are compared with the shared catalog, which lives only on the owner machine; the shell self-test holds the embedded bytes to PROVENANCE.txt on every build.
Every package carries THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt, written by hand; the gate holds its module sections to what each shipped executable links.
DOC-INTERNAL-QUALITY rules 1-3 and 5-7: the document registry both ways, relative links and anchors, house style and offline safety of the internal corpus, on every local build gate.
DOC-INTERNAL-QUALITY rule 4: the check flag and FILEDO_CHECK_* tables in the READMEs and the filedo_check option table are held to the parser inside the cmd/filedo suite.

DOC-EXTERNAL-QUALITY rules 1-7 over the published site and the READMEs: glossary and subject index, sitemap against the page set, SEO block, locale completeness and translation freshness, termbase, screenshots and prose hygiene, on every local build gate.

Re-takes the guide screenshots from the GUI and the MSI; it opens windows on the desktop, so the maintainer runs it after a GUI page or the installer feature tree changes. check-external-docs.ps1 holds the committed pictures (present, sized, alt text) on every build.

A build input that git ignores passes every local step and is missing from the checkout the tagged run builds; the gate fails on any glyph, icon, source, project or installer file that is on disk, untracked and ignored.
The FMS worker client is linked into filedo.exe; its tests (pipe-server identity, response limits, drain consent) run in the local gate and the release workflow.
A Go package with tests that no gate runs ships regressions green; the check requires every such package to be gated in build.ps1 and release.yml or exempt with a reason.

Writes a dated metrics checkpoint of the free promotion campaign from public or owner-held counters only; the maintainer runs it by hand at each checkpoint (at most fourteen days apart while outreach is active) because it needs the owner's gh login and the network, so no gate runs it.

Writes docs/sitemap.xml from the public page set and the page files' commit dates; the maintainer runs it whenever a public page is added, changed or committed, and its -Check switch compares the page set with the file. The external-docs gate holds the result to the page set on every build gate, so no gate runs the generator itself.

ticket: winget PR checklist (owner rule 2026-10-07), recorded by the SP-0166 review
reason: Ticks the winget-pkgs PR template item by item, on evidence, after release.ps1 opens the PR; it needs the owner's gh login and the network, so no local gate runs it.

CONTEXT-HELP section 4 rung 1, static half: the generated in-app help set docs/help - map, pages in every shipped language, links, no request - on every local build gate (gate step help-pages). Its -Exe half needs a desktop session and runs before a release.

The pre-release operations run: every kind of filedo operation on small data with the shipped exe_to_download\filedo.exe, each step timed and byte-checked and the whole run compared with the last passing runs (function, speed, verb coverage). release.ps1 runs it before the tag; it is not in the local gate because its mounted tier needs administrator rights (one UAC prompt, or release.ps1 -SkipOpsMount) and its load section sizes the data so that each step runs for seconds.

The speed gate of prove-operations.ps1 tested on its own (functions lifted by AST, synthetic rows and baselines, no filedo run and no disk, about a second; exit 1 when a threshold test fails). RELEASE.md tells the maintainer to change a threshold and this file in the same edit; no gate runs it, so that remains a review rule. It is cheap enough to join the local gate if the owner wants it there.

Live proof of partition disks (SP-0148) on disposable VHDX disks it creates and deletes itself, never a disk of the machine; it needs an elevated session (it asks for consent once) and the Hyper-V module, so the maintainer runs it by hand when the partition carrier changes. Evidence goes to the git-ignored temp\evidence folder. No tracked document names it.

Live proof of the brokered (unelevated) path of partition disks (SP-0148 section 8) on a disposable VHDX: every filedo command runs unelevated and Windows asks for consent at each step, with two short elevated phases that make and remove the VHDX. A person answers the prompts, so no gate can run it; the maintainer runs it by hand. No tracked document names it.
runnerToken: Run from an ordinary, NOT elevated PowerShell

reason: Live proof of the stale-row cleanup and the keep-alive watcher (vd mount keep): it kills a block server and waits for the watcher to bring the disk back, on a scratch 64 MB container; it needs an elevated session. The maintainer runs it by hand after a change to the mount watcher. No tracked document names it.

The machine-changing proofs for MSI versioning and upgrades (PKG-01) and the setup EXE Modify and upgrade path (PKG-02): it installs and removes FileDO on the machine it runs on, elevated, over a built pair, a later same-day pair and the last published pair. The build gate only reads the installer versions back from the built files (build.ps1); this update-over-prior proof stays a release-time hand run. No tracked document names it.
runnerToken: ELEVATED, and it installs and removes FileDO

reason: Screenshots a FileDO window on a named display for the DPI proofs (SP-0016 T4): it needs a desktop session with the display in question, moves a real window and snapshots then restores HKCU\Software\FileDO. A proof aid for the maintainer, not a pass-or-fail check; no gate can run it.
runnerToken: Close any open FileDO window first

reason: Reads or changes the scaling of one display so the DPI proofs can run at a scale no display here has. It changes the user desktop, so whoever calls it puts the old value back (capture-dpi callers do it in a finally block); a helper of the manual DPI proofs, not a check, and no gate can run it.
runnerToken: Read or change the scaling of one display

reason: Own Go module (cmd/filedo-check/go.mod), so neither the root go test nor check-gated-packages.ps1 sees it. Its main_test.go pins every documented command line of filedo_check to the exact filedo.exe argv and the launcher suite shared with the other companions proves exit-code and argv forwarding, exit 2 with no filedo.exe, no current-folder or PATH lookup, the symlink case and Ctrl+Break. No gate ran it until SP-0171 W6; the compile-test-module step now runs it from inside the module on every local build gate.

Its main_test.go pins every documented command line of filedo_fill to the exact filedo.exe argv and the launcher suite shared with the other companions proves exit-code and argv forwarding, exit 2 with no filedo.exe, no current-folder or PATH lookup, the symlink case and Ctrl+Break. The runner of the tests/*.lst scenario lists (recorded above under tests/*.lst): it renders their placeholders from FILEDO_TEST_TARGET after refusing anything that is not disposable (a mounted virtual disk that is not the system drive, or a folder under %TEMP%) and runs filedo against the rendered copy. Operator-driven by design, so no gate runs it.
